island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland, Australia

abs_area.note: The ABS locality is gazetted as Amity; locals and every sign on the island say Amity Point.

honesty: The census_baseline block is real published ABS 2021 Census data with the source URL on every table. Everything else in this file is a modelling construct built on top of it.

No household archetype, occupation or visitor archetype describes a real person or a real family. They are types, not people, and none of them should ever be shown to a player as a portrait of someone who lives here.
Every share_of_households_estimate, every pay figure and every hour-by-hour rhythm is an estimate for the simulation to run on. None of them is measured. Do not display them to a player as fact.

Percentages from ABS QuickStats are used in preference to raw counts. The raw occupied and unoccupied dwelling counts we could read off the QuickStats pages did not reconcile with the published totals, so counts in this file are derived from the published percentages and are marked derived.
The name pools are common Australian names chosen so that no combination reads as a real islander. They deliberately exclude every surname that appears anywhere in businesses.json or places.json.

Nothing cultural is asserted here. Quandamooka households appear in this file only through public census facts and public employment facts. Ceremony, language, kinship and protocol are not modelled and must not be generated: they go to docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md and to QYAC.

census_baseline.collection: Australian Census of Population and Housing, 10 August 2021
census_baseline.why_it_matters: A census night in August is the island at its emptiest. Half the dwellings are holiday houses and the campgrounds are quiet. Every visitor number in this file has to be added on top of this baseline, never read out of it.

indigenous.note: Queensland was 4.6 per cent at the same census. This island is more than three times the state share, and the Indigenous median age is twelve years younger than the island median.

dwellings.note: Half the island's houses had nobody in them on census night. Queensland's figure was 9.3 per cent. This single number is the island's economy, its housing shortage and its politics in one line.

tenure_pct.note: Owned outright is well above the Queensland figure of 29.1 per cent and mortgages well below 34.4 per cent. An island of paid-off houses and a thin, expensive rental market.

income.median_monthly_mortgage_note: The island figure we read equals the Queensland figure exactly, which is what a mis-read of the comparison column would look like. Treat as unverified until someone opens the ABS table directly.

industry_top_responses_pct.note: These are ABS fine-level industry classes, not divisions. Mineral sand mining still shows at 4.9 per cent because the 2021 census was taken during the rehabilitation phase after mining ended in December 2019; it should be modelled as shrinking, not stable.

travel_to_work_pct.note: About one worker in twenty drives to a ferry and crosses the bay to a mainland job. Worked at home at 16.8 per cent is high, and that census fell in a COVID year, so treat it as a ceiling rather than a steady state.

island.age_shape_note: The 60 to 74 band alone is 29.5 per cent of the island. The 20 to 34 band is 11.4 per cent. Any agent population that looks like a normal Australian town is wrong for this place.

townships.name: Dunwich (Goompi)
townships.character: The working town and the front door. Highest Indigenous share on the island by a wide margin, the youngest median age of the three, the most renting, the most services, and the only township where the ferry, the barge, the school, the health service and the council depot all sit within a few streets of each other.

townships.name: Point Lookout (Mulumba)
townships.character: Two thirds of the houses are empty on a winter Tuesday and full at Christmas. The oldest median age, the highest incomes, the lowest Indigenous share, and the township whose population swings hardest between a wet June week and the first week of January.

townships.name: Amity Point (Pulan)
townships.character: The oldest and the poorest of the three: median age 58, median household income $931 a week, half the houses owned outright, one in five workers a labourer. A quiet fishing and retirement village that also has to live with a shoreline that keeps moving.

derived_for_simulation.note: Township occupied counts derived from each locality's published percentage of its own private dwellings. They fall about 97 short of the island total, which is the balance living outside the three gazetted localities (One Mile and scattered rural addresses). The residual is carried openly rather than smoothed away.

unoccupied_dwelling_coverage.note: The two dwelling-only archetypes in this pack account for about 81 per cent of the island's unoccupied stock, concentrated at Point Lookout and Amity Point. The remaining fifth is mostly Dunwich, where a quarter of dwellings were unoccupied on census night for ordinary reasons: between tenancies, on the market, being repaired, or the occupant was away. There is no holiday-home archetype for Dunwich because that is not what Dunwich's empty houses are.

derived_for_simulation.swing_note: Peak visitor load is not published. Businesses.json carries per-business peak multipliers between 1.0 and 3.5. Model the January and Easter island as the 2,156 residents plus a visitor population in the thousands, and treat any specific peak headcount as unmeasured.

caveats: 2021 is five years stale as at 2026 and it was a COVID census. Work-from-home is inflated, mineral sand mining is a fading tail, and short-stay letting has moved since.
Occupied and unoccupied dwelling counts are derived from published percentages, not read as counts.
The island median monthly mortgage is flagged low confidence; see the note on that field.
There is no published township-level breakdown of visitor numbers, staff housing, or how many workers live on the mainland and cross daily.

interest_groups.label: Quandamooka families
interest_groups.about: Traditional Owner households and the community around QYAC, QALSMA, Yulu-Burri-Ba and MMEIC. Cares about joint management of Country, Native Title outcomes, employment on Country, housing and health.
interest_groups.civic_weight_note: 16.1 per cent of residents island-wide and 30.5 per cent in Dunwich, so this group's weight is township-dependent and must never be averaged away.
interest_groups.note: This is a civic constituency label for the simulation. It is not a cultural authority and does not speak for QYAC.

interest_groups.label: Long-term residents
interest_groups.about: People who have lived here through the mine closing and the tourism turn. Cares about the cost of the ferry, the state of the roads, whether services stay open in winter, and being consulted before things change.

interest_groups.label: Holiday home owners
interest_groups.about: Ratepayers who are here six to thirty nights a year. Cares about rates, parking, amenity, dogs and noise, and about anything that touches the value or lettability of a second home.
interest_groups.note: Backed by the hardest number in the pack: 50.3 per cent of private dwellings unoccupied on census night, 65 per cent at Point Lookout.

interest_groups.label: Tourism and hospitality operators
interest_groups.about: Accommodation, cafes, tours, dive and surf schools, the pub and the clubs. Cares about ferry capacity, staff housing, trading hours, event permits and anything that moves visitor volume.

interest_groups.label: Renters and key workers
interest_groups.about: The chefs, nurses, teachers, cleaners and deckhands who need a bed on the island. Cares about rental supply, short-stay letting rules, worker accommodation and the last boat home.
interest_groups.note: 26.4 per cent of occupied dwellings rented island-wide, 30.7 per cent in Dunwich, against 50 per cent of all dwellings sitting empty.

interest_groups.label: Retirees and seniors
interest_groups.about: The largest single bloc on the island. Cares about health access, transport to appointments, footpaths, the pool, the clubs, rates relief and emergency response times.
interest_groups.note: Median age 52; 29.5 per cent of residents are 60 to 74.

interest_groups.label: Young families and the school
interest_groups.about: Households with children at Dunwich State School or crossing to Cleveland for high school. Cares about the ferry timetable, school transport subsidies, the pool, sport, childcare and youth activities.

interest_groups.label: Trades and builders
interest_groups.about: Island-based trades plus the mainland crews who barge over. Cares about barge bookings and freight cost, development approvals, the tip, and parking a ute and trailer.
interest_groups.note: Technicians and trades 12.5 per cent island-wide, labourers 15.8 per cent and 20.9 per cent at Amity Point.

interest_groups.label: Environmental stewards
interest_groups.about: Bushcare, wildlife rescue, dune care, the people who count koalas and pull weeds. Cares about dune damage, beach driving, feral animals, water in the lakes, fire management and the national park.

interest_groups.label: Fishers and boaties
interest_groups.about: Recreational and commercial fishers, the fishing club, VMR volunteers, ramp and jetty users. Cares about ramp access and parking, channel markers, closures, shark policy and fuel price.

interest_groups.label: Surfers and beach users
interest_groups.about: Dawn patrol locals, the surf club, swimmers, and the four-wheel-drive beach crowd. Cares about patrol hours, beach vehicle permits, camping rules, gorge walk crowding and parking.

interest_groups.label: Volunteers and emergency services
interest_groups.about: Rural fire brigade, VMR, surf life saving, wildlife rescue, club committees and hall volunteers. Cares about training, equipment, insurance, the age of the volunteer base and burnout.
interest_groups.note: On an island with one ambulance station and a police station in Dunwich, the volunteer base is not a nice-to-have. It is the second half of the emergency system.

interest_groups.label: Ferry commuters
interest_groups.about: Workers and students who cross the bay most days. Cares about the first and last service, fare and vehicle cost, terminal parking, cancellations in weather and the school transport subsidy.

policy: Common Australian given names and surnames only.

Every surname in this pool was checked against every name string in data/businesses.json and data/places.json and any collision was removed. The check is a script, not a promise; re-run it when either pack changes.
No agent may be given the name of a real islander. If a generated name matches a real local, it is a bug, and the fix is to remove the name from the pool, not to keep it because it was random.
Never attach a generated name to a real organisation's real role. There is no named QYAC chief executive, no named school principal, no named publican in this world.

Names carry no cultural information. Do not generate Quandamooka names, skin names, totems or family lines. Quandamooka households in this file are census facts and job facts only, and anything further goes through docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md.
name_pools.note: Given names are grouped by the decade a person of that age would plausibly have been named in, because an island with a median age of 52 should not be full of agents named like a 2020s prep class.

nicknames.note: Australian usage. About one adult in three on this island would be introduced by a shortened name rather than a given name. Apply to residents, rarely to visitors.
pattern: trade or boat name, for example 'the sparky' or 'Toots off the barge'
nicknames.warning: Never generate a nickname that could identify a real local. If it sounds like someone, drop it.

household_naming.rule: Households are labelled by archetype id plus a generated surname, for example 'the Fenwick house, retired-owner-couple-point-lookout'. Never label a household with a real family name.

occupations.bad_day: A southerly, a full standby list, a caravan that will not fit the deck plan, and forty people who all believe they were promised the next boat.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.bad_day: A cancelled sailing and a car park that becomes a waiting room.

occupations.what_it_is: Runs a pub, club or tavern: rosters, stock, compliance, live music, functions and the room at midnight.
occupations.typical_week: Six days, late nights, every holiday.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A packed room, a band that lands, and no incident report.
occupations.bad_day: Two staff short, a delivery that missed the barge, and a crowd that is not going home.

occupations.label: Grocery and retail assistant
occupations.what_it_is: Registers, shelves, deliveries and the fact that this shop is the only shop, so its stock levels are a public issue.
occupations.typical_week: Rostered across seven days, heaviest on ferry days and Fridays.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: Full shelves, a truck that came, and a steady stream of people you know.
occupations.bad_day: No barge, no milk, no bread, and a queue explaining to you that this is unacceptable.

occupations.label: Primary school teacher
occupations.what_it_is: Teaches at the island's only school, Prep to Year 6, in a community where you will meet every parent at the shop.
occupations.typical_week: Term time, 8am to well past 4pm, plus camps, sport and community events.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A kid reads something they could not read in March.
occupations.bad_day: A hard family situation you cannot leave at work in a town this size.

occupations.label: Teacher aide
occupations.what_it_is: Classroom support, often a local parent, often the person who holds the relationship with a struggling child's family.
occupations.typical_week: School hours, term time, part-time hours.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

seasonality.winter_risk: no paid hours in school holidays

occupations.good_day: A breakthrough with the child everyone had given up on this week.
occupations.bad_day: Hours cut, or a child you cannot help because the service is on the mainland.

occupations.label: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health worker
occupations.what_it_is: Community-controlled primary health care: chronic disease, social and emotional wellbeing, transport, follow-up and the trust that makes any of it work.
occupations.typical_week: Weekday clinic hours, plus outreach and a load of unrostered community contact.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

seasonality.winter_risk: none; resident load, not visitor load

occupations.good_day: Someone who has avoided the clinic for two years walks in.
occupations.bad_day: A death in a small community where you knew the family and everyone else you see that day did too.

occupations.label: Practice or clinic nurse
occupations.what_it_is: General practice and outpost nursing on an island where the nearest hospital is across the bay.
occupations.typical_week: Weekday clinic hours with the constant awareness that the transfer options are a boat and a helicopter.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A busy clinic that runs to time and nothing that needed a helicopter.
occupations.bad_day: A cardiac case at 6pm with the last ferry gone.

occupations.label: General practitioner
occupations.what_it_is: The island's doctor. Sees residents and a summer flood of visitors with sunburn, cuts, stings and things they should have seen someone about last week.
occupations.typical_week: Clinic days, often not five, sometimes a locum on rotation.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage. GP earnings vary enormously with billing model; this is a wide modelling band only.

occupations.good_day: Nothing walks in that the island cannot handle.
occupations.bad_day: Something does, in a southerly, with the boats stopped.

occupations.label: Paramedic
occupations.what_it_is: Ambulance response on an island where transfer to a hospital means a barge or a helicopter, and where you will know the patient.
occupations.typical_week: Twelve-hour shifts on a rotating roster including nights.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A good outcome on a job you would not have got in the city.
occupations.bad_day: A drowning, a road crash, or a long wait for a retrieval in bad weather.

occupations.label: Police officer
occupations.what_it_is: Small station policing: traffic, alcohol, domestic incidents, missing persons, marine and beach incidents, and holiday crowds that outnumber the town.
occupations.typical_week: Rostered shifts, thin numbers, and everyone knows where you live.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A quiet shift and a found child returned to a car park full of relieved people.
occupations.bad_day: Schoolies week energy in a town with one road and a beach full of vehicles.

occupations.label: Aged and disability support worker
occupations.what_it_is: In-home personal care, meals, transport and company for older and disabled islanders, driving between clients across three townships.
occupations.typical_week: Split shifts, mornings and evenings, seven days, with a lot of unpaid travel time inside them.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

seasonality.winter_risk: none; the steadiest work on the island

requirements: certificate III in individual support or equivalent
occupations.good_day: Everyone showered, fed, and someone laughed.
occupations.bad_day: A client on the floor, and twenty-five minutes of driving between you and the next one.

occupations.label: Builder or carpenter, island-based
occupations.what_it_is: Renovations, decks, storm repairs and new builds, with every stick of material arriving on a barge.
occupations.typical_week: Six-thirty start, off the tools mid afternoon, quotes and ordering at night.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage. Charge-out for a sole trader, which is not take-home.

seasonality.winter_risk: none, but December to January is dead because owners are in the houses

occupations.good_day: Everything turned up on the barge and the frame is up by three.
occupations.bad_day: A missed barge booking, a certifier on the mainland, and a client who has decided to move a wall.

occupations.label: Mainland tradesperson, working the island
occupations.what_it_is: Specialist trades that the island does not carry full time: refrigeration, lifts, electrical inspection, plant maintenance. Comes over for the day with a loaded ute.
occupations.typical_week: One or two island days a fortnight, sized to fit between the first and last barge.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage. Charge-out including a barge fare and the travel time, which is why island jobs cost what they do.

occupations.good_day: Three jobs done, back on the 3:30.
occupations.bad_day: The part is wrong, the shop is on the mainland, and the next boat with space is tomorrow.

occupations.label: Council outdoor worker
occupations.what_it_is: Parks, roads, drains, public toilets, beach access tracks and the bins that triple in weight in January.
occupations.typical_week: Early weekday starts, with a holiday-period cleaning load that is a different job entirely.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: Beach access repaired before the weekend and nobody complains, which counts as thanks.
occupations.bad_day: Every bin overflowing, a blocked toilet block, and a public holiday roster.

occupations.what_it_is: Runs the island's tip and recycling centre: the single choke point for everything the island throws away and everything the trades cannot bury.
occupations.typical_week: Open days only, and every trade on the island times its afternoon around them.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A quiet Tuesday and a full salvage shelf.
occupations.bad_day: The day after a long weekend.

occupations.label: Mine rehabilitation and land management worker
occupations.what_it_is: Earthworks, revegetation and monitoring on the old mine leases. What is left of a seventy-year industry, and shrinking.

pay_band.note: Indicative only. A modelling band, not a quoted award rate, not an advertised wage.

occupations.good_day: A revegetated block that has taken, three years after you seeded it.
occupations.bad_day: A contract that ends with nothing behind it.

occupations.what_it_is: Works the bay and the passage, and sells at the door or through a local outlet.

occupations.good_day: Whales off the gorge and a group that listens.
occupations.bad_day: A bogged vehicle on a rising tide.

occupations.label: Artist or maker

measured_baseline.caveat: Reported in 2019 for the 2018 year, in 2018 dollars. Not adjusted, not current, and no more recent public figure was found. Every share_of_visitors_estimate below is a modelling split of this total, not measured segmentation.

how_to_use_this_pack: Sample households from household_archetypes using share_of_households_estimate as a weight, until the township targets in census_baseline.derived_for_simulation are met. Do not sample the two archetypes with tenure 'not_a_residence' into the resident population: they occupy dwellings from target_unoccupied_dwellings using share_of_unoccupied_dwellings_estimate.
Draw ages from census_baseline.island.age_distribution, not from a generic curve. This island's shape is the point.
Draw names from name_pools by the era that matches the agent's age. Check every generated name against the pool policy before it is displayed.
Assign occupations from the household's work list. Cross-check the employer ids against data/businesses.json and drop any employer whose status is 'closed' or 'proposed'.
Use rhythm blocks as intentions, not as a script. An agent that is hungry, sick, rostered off or stuck behind a ferry queue should break its rhythm, and the break is where the drama is.
Peak season is not a multiplier on residents. It is a separate visitor population layered on top, drawn from visitor_archetypes.
Determinism: draw every sample from world.rng.stream('residents'). Never Math.random.
instantiation.civic_hook: cares_about maps a household to interest group ids. When a civic lever moves, weight the reaction by the household's share and by the group weight. The two archetypes with tenure 'not_a_residence' vote nowhere and pay rates, which is the whole shape of the island's civic argument.
drama_hooks: A lease ends in October and a family with two kids has nowhere to go while 65 per cent of the houses in their township sit empty.
The last boat goes and someone who needed to be on it is not.
A support worker leaves the island because they could not find a rental, and four older residents lose their morning call.
A cook works sixty hours in January and twenty in June, and the difference is the rent.
A high schooler misses the water taxi and the whole day falls apart.
An ambulance job needs a hospital and the weather has stopped the boats.
do_not: Do not name a resident agent after a real islander, or give an agent a real person's role at a real organisation.
Do not generate cultural content for any household. Quandamooka households in this pack are census facts and public job types only.
Do not present any pay figure, share, or rhythm in this file to a player as measured fact.
Do not add the visitor population to the resident population in any published figure.
